title: Fusion-aware kernel planner for INT8/FP8 fast paths and dequant elimination
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Design and implement a fusion-aware kernel planning layer that selects and schedules fused INT8/FP8 attention + epilogue kernels to avoid redundant dequant/quant roundtrips during prefill and decode. The planner should consider sequence length distribution, prefix reuse (KV cache hit ratios), batch stride, and memory bandwidth to choose between: (1) fused INT8 attention kernels that operate directly on quantized weights+activations, (2) mixed-precision FP8 paths for layers flagged as numerical-sensitive, and (3) a safe dequant+FP32 attention fallback when numerical regression risk is high. Primary goal: reduce dequant overhead and memory copies on common PLG workloads while keeping output quality regressions below defined thresholds.
acceptance_criteria: End-to-end inference with fused INT8 attention kernels shows >=20% reduction in per-token CPU+GPU memory bandwidth compared to current INT8 path with explicit dequant copies on our microbench harness for seq=128, batch=8.
Latency P95 for decode with prefix reuse (KV hit > 70%) improves by >=12% without increasing tail variance beyond 3%.
Automated numeric regression tests (RMS and pass/fail token-level checks) detect no regression vs baseline FP32 above configured thresholds for high-sensitivity prompts.
Fallback to safe dequant+FP32 path when a model-layer is marked incompatible with fused kernels, with observable rollout metrics in console.
Comprehensive unit and integration tests added; CI perf jobs report stable results within noise for the past 5 runs.
benchmark_summary: Initial local microbench: fused INT8+epilogue kernel reduces host->device memcpy by ~28% and overall token/sec for decode increases from 10.8k to 12.4k on A100 for seq=128,batch=8. Mixed FP8 path shows smaller memory wins but better numerical stability on layer types flagged by model on-boarding. Compiler selection heuristics cut kernel-switch jitter at runtime by selecting kernels predicated on median sequence length per route.
implementation_notes: Add kernel metadata table with: stable kernel id, precision (INT8/FP8/FP32), fuse-capabilities (attention+epilogue, prefill-only optimizations), and per-kernel memory footprint estimates.
Extend planner to consume runtime signals: median_seq_len, kv_cache_hit_ratio, batch_stride, and recent per-route tail-latency histograms.
Implement a dequant-elimination pass that rewrites prefill pipelines to use fused kernels when model quantization map allows contiguous int8 layouts.
Performance guardrails: a soft threshold for KV hit ratio (<30%) disables prefill fusion to prevent increased decode latency on cold-prefix workloads.
Add a runtime metric 'quant_fusion_offers' and 'quant_fusion_taken' to Console and link to per-route dashboards for observability.
rollout_plan: Phase 1: Feature gated behind runtime flag; internal canary on small set of routes (non-critical, high-traffic dev org) for two weeks.
Phase 2: Broader beta to customers with opt-in SDK flag and console toggle; collect numeric regressions and perf histograms for 72h windows.
Phase 3: Gradual default enable for hosted routes with auto-fallback if numeric regressions or tail-latency rise beyond thresholds.
Rollout observability: dashboard with perf delta, numeric-regression alerts, and per-route fallback counts.
blockers: Need validated model quantization maps from model-onboarding (research) to safely classify layers as fusion-compatible.
GPU kernel PR review backlog (internal runtime repo) blocking merged fused kernels required by planner.
Numerical regression harness needs extension for new mixed FP8 golden traces.
